title: Why ‘Unwritten Rules’ Die Hard
text:
Why ‘Unwritten Rules’ Die Hard

Christopher Beddor

Gavekal Dragonomics | 27 Nov 2026

The theme that ties together many of top leader Xi Jinping’s recent priorities and campaigns is a desire to crack down on the “unwritten rules” of the Communist Party and government. These refer to the practices and strategies that underpin bureaucratic life in China: myriad informal rules about how to trade favors, find powerful political patrons or bend directives from above. According to Xi, these cynical behaviors and norms are “invisible yet everywhere… and have become a deep-rooted cancer that corrupts Party members and officials, and poisons the Party’s culture."The anti-corruption campaign targets practices such as accepting banquet invitations and gifts in exchange for favors, helping protégés to secure promotions and improperly intervening in government operations (see Anti-Corruption After The Plenum). A separate campaign this year on “taking the correct view of political performance” similarly targets officials who attempt to climb the hierarchy through self-serving investments in wasteful projects that are designed to impress leaders (see Pressure Builds On Local Officials). And both campaigns aim to centralize decision-making authority by targeting lower-level officials who fail to implement the leadership’s instructions.
